docs.title: K-CURE Data Documentation
docs.text: Welcome. This site is an unofficial guide to the cancer and health data released through K-CURE (케이큐어), the health and medical data portal of the Korean Ministry of Health and Welfare (보건복지부).

docs.title: Motivation
docs.text:
K-CURE is the route to the Korea Central Cancer Registry (중앙암등록본부) linked to claims, screening, and death records. The registry records who was diagnosed, with which cancer, and at what stage. The linked files record the care before and after that diagnosis. A registry diagnosis is a reported cancer, so the combination supports studies that a billing code alone would leave uncertain.

The official documentation is in Korean and spread across portal pages, data catalogs, and a separate data dictionary. This site brings it together in English, with the Korean terms kept beside the English.

It is modeled on the NHIS Data Documentation and on the documentation that the Research Data Assistance Center (ResDAC) provides for Medicare data.

docs.title: What is on this site
docs.text:
The site has six parts.

  • Program and data describes the project, the products on the portal, the application, and where the data are analyzed.
  • Datasets has one page per table of the Cancer Public Library, and a sample page for the site samples (표본) and staging samples (표본 병기).
  • Variables lists the variables of every table, first for the customized extract and then for each sample, with a page per variable.
  • Research notes is a set of posts on working with the data. The first explains how the tables fit together.
  • Glossary translates the Korean terms used on the portal and in the registry.
  • References lists the profile paper and the official pages these entries follow.

docs.title: Where to start
docs.text: Start with the Cancer Public Library page. The registry is the table RGST, and claims, screening, and death are the other tables. A study of one cancer site that needs detailed stage, such as tumor size, nodes, and metastasis, should look at the staging samples. The research note on how the tables fit together explains the joins.

docs.title: Disclaimer
docs.text: This site is not affiliated with or endorsed by the Ministry of Health and Welfare, the Korea Health Information Service (한국보건의료정보원), the National Cancer Center (국립암센터), or the National Cancer Data Center (국가암데이터센터). Entries are written from public sources and may contain errors, so check them against the dictionary and the extract that come with an approved project.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text:
Corrections and additions are welcome from anyone who has worked with the data. The easiest way to send them is an email to sihopark@kdischool.ac.kr. The contributing page explains what to include.

Maintained by Siho Park, KDI School of Public Policy and Management.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text: The portal and the official manuals use Korean administrative terms. This page gives the English used on this site, so that one Korean term keeps one English translation. Claims terms that also appear in the NHIS databases are defined in more detail in the NHIS glossary.

docs.title: Related documentation
docs.text: NHIS Data Documentation covers the National Health Insurance Service research databases. Those databases share claims, eligibility, and screening concepts with the public library, and they are a different extract.

docs.title: How to cite
docs.text:
If this site helped your research, please cite it as follows.

Park, Siho. K-CURE Data Documentation. https://siho-park.github.io/kcure-documentation/. Accessed [date].

For the Cancer Public Library, also cite the data resource profile, which describes the first release:

Choi DW, Guk MY, Kim HR, Ryu KS, Kong HJ, Cha HS, Kim HJ, Chae H, Jeon YS, Kim H, Jung J, Im JS, Choi KS. Data Resource Profile: The Cancer Public Library Database in South Korea. Cancer Research and Treatment. 2024;56(4):1014-1026. https://doi.org/10.4143/crt.2024.207

Later releases cover more years than that profile. The version actually used should be named from the data dictionary supplied with the extract. The sources and versions page lists the public descriptions of those later releases.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: Contributions from researchers who have used the data are what make this site useful. A correction to a single code, or a note that two official pages disagree, saves the next user the same afternoon of detective work.

docs.title: Suggesting a correction
docs.text: The simplest way to suggest a change is an email to sihopark@kdischool.ac.kr. Please include the link to the page, the change you propose, and its source if there is one, such as a manual, a published paper, or your own experience with the data.

docs.title: Using GitHub
docs.text:
Contributors who use GitHub can also suggest a change there directly.

  • Open an issue. Describe the problem or the missing information in a GitHub issue.
  • Edit the page. Every page has an edit button at the top right that opens its source file on GitHub, where you can propose the change as a pull request.

docs.title: Writing a post
docs.text: Researchers who have worked with the data are welcome to write a post for Research notes. A post can be short and cover a single pitfall, a way of constructing a variable, or a lesson from the application or export process. Send the draft by email to sihopark@kdischool.ac.kr in any format, such as Word, Google Docs, or plain text, together with your name and affiliation as they should appear on the post. The draft is then formatted for the site and published under your name.

docs.title: What not to post
docs.text: Never post individual-level records, screenshots of the analysis environment, or statistics computed from the data that have not passed export review (반출심사). Describing the structure of a variable, its codes, and its pitfalls is fine. Numbers from the data should be limited to results that have already been cleared for release, such as published tables.

docs.title: Variable pages
docs.text: The Variables pages are generated from data dictionary version 4.0 (자료설명서) and the portal's data catalogs. A correction to a variable page is best sent with the page and line of the dictionary or catalog that supports it.

docs.title: Research notes
docs.text:
These posts cover the practical side of the K-CURE data, from merging the tables to the caveats that the variable lists leave to the dictionary. They are written for researchers who are new to the data, and each post can be read on its own.

Researchers who have worked with the data are welcome to share what they have learned, and a post can be as short as a single pitfall. Send a draft in any format to sihopark@kdischool.ac.kr, as described on the contributing page.

docs.title: How the K-CURE tables fit together
docs.text: The Cancer Public Library (암 공공 라이브러리) arrives as a set of separate tables. A project that follows a person from screening through diagnosis, treatment, and death starts by joining those tables. This post says what one row of each table stands for, names the person identifier, and lists the joins that connect the tables. The variable lists are in Variables. The table pages are under Cancer Public Library.

docs.title: What one row stands for
docs.text:
The library is one database. A customized extract uses the tables below. A site sample and a staging sample are separate databases, with their own file names and shorter column lists. Several files are the same kind of record split by year, because the questionnaire changed. Those year files still identify a person with the same key.

Tables 한글 One row RGST 암등록 One registered cancer, 2012–2022. A person with two cancers has two rows DEATH 사망 One death, 2012–2023. A person who is alive has no row BFC 자격 및 보험료 One person in one year, 2007–2024, if that person still had eligibility on 31 December T200 명세서 일반내역 One claim, 2007–2024 T300 진료내역 One service line on a claim T400 상병내역 One diagnosis on a claim T530 원외처방내역 One outpatient prescription line G1E_OBJ 일반건강검진 대상자 One person in the checkup target file for an examination year G1Q_0708, G1Q_0917, G1Q_1824 일반건강검진 문진 One checkup questionnaire. The file is 2007–2008, 2009–2017, or 2018–2024 G1E 일반건강검진 결과 One checkup result, 2007–2024 CQ, and CBR, CCR, CCX, CLV, CST 암검진 One screening record. Each site has a 2007–2008 file and a 2009–2024 file. CQ holds the questionnaire items shared across sites COVID_PT 코로나19 확진자 One confirmed case, 2020 through 31 August 2023 COVID_VAC 코로나19 예방접종 One vaccination, 17 December 2020 through 31 August 2023

T200 is the hub of the claims. It carries the person, the start and end of care, the provider, and the reviewed amounts. T300, T400, and T530 add the lines of that claim.

docs.title: The person identifier
docs.text:
The person identifier is SN_KEY (대체식별키).

Variable 한글 English Where it appears SN_KEY 대체식별키 Person identifier Every table in the Cancer Public Library

Dictionary version 4.0, section 10, links the whole file from the five institutions on this substitute identifier: cancer registration, death, eligibility and premium, health examinations, cancer screening, and COVID-19, and the claims tables as well. It is the first variable on each list in Variables. The page for the cancer-registration copy is here.

Two facts about SN_KEY decide how a merge behaves.

  • A person with two registered cancers has two rows on RGST and the same SN_KEY on both. Joining RGST to another table on SN_KEY repeats the other table's rows once for each cancer.
  • The quality-control section of the dictionary says each table's substitute identifier is replaced with a new serial number every time the data are extracted. An SN_KEY from one extract does not identify the same person in another extract.

docs.title: Joins that cover most analyses
docs.text:
• A person across the library. Join any table to any other table on SN_KEY. Death, province of residence (BFC.SIDO_CD), and the registry stage (RGST.SEER_GRP) all meet on that key.
  • The lines of a claim. Join T300, T400, and T530 to T200 on MID (명세서조인키). The dictionary describes MID as the substitute identifier that builds one claim from the four tables. Dates of care, the provider, and the reviewed amounts sit on T200, so a service line or a diagnosis reaches them through MID.
  • Eligibility for the year of a claim. BFC has one row per person per year, in STD_YYYY. T200 dates the claim with RECU_FR_DD (요양개시일자). Match SN_KEY, and match the year of RECU_FR_DD to STD_YYYY.
  • A checkup. The questionnaire for 2018–2024 is G1Q_1824, for 2009–2017 is G1Q_0917, and for 2007–2008 is G1Q_0708. The measured results are on G1E for the whole period. Join the questionnaire file for that year to G1E on SN_KEY and EXMD_BZ_YYYY.
  • A cancer screening. The site file (CBR, CCR, CCX, CLV, or CST) joins to the shared questionnaire CQ on SN_KEY and EXMD_BZ_YYYY, using the 2007–2008 pair or the 2009–2024 pair.
  • COVID-19. COVID_PT and COVID_VAC join to the registry on SN_KEY. Vaccination has one row per dose, so a person can have several rows.

docs.title: Joining two claim-detail tables
docs.text:
T300, T400, and T530 each have many rows for one MID. Joining T300 to T400 on MID pairs every service line with every diagnosis on that claim. A claim with three diagnoses and ten service lines becomes thirty rows, and a sum of service-line amounts is then counted three times.

The pattern that keeps one row per claim is to collapse each detail table first, for example to an indicator for a diagnosis or a total amount per MID, and then join that result to T200. A join that adds information about claims should leave the number of claims unchanged. Counting the rows before and after the join is the check.

docs.title: Datasets
docs.text:
The Cancer Public Library (암 공공 라이브러리) starts from the national cancer registry and attaches death, eligibility, claims, checkups, screening, and COVID-19 records to the same people. It is released as three separate databases: a customized extract, a site sample, and a staging sample.

At a glance

  • Three databases. A customized extract covers every registered cancer from 2012 to 2022. A site sample covers about 20 percent of one cancer site, and a staging sample covers about 10 percent of one site, with detailed stage.
  • Tables. The customized extract has 26 tables, all joined on the person identifier SN_KEY.
  • One row per cancer. A row of RGST is one registered cancer, so a person with two cancers has two rows.
  • Other products. The clinical library, specialized data, and health data are separate databases with their own documentation.
Sources

The table list follows data dictionary version 4.0 (September 2026). The samples follow the portal's data catalogs, downloaded 30 October 2026, and the K-CURE library overview. Where official figures differ, they are lined up on Sources and versions.

docs.title: Other products
docs.text:
These are separate databases, described briefly on their own pages.

  • The clinical library (임상 라이브러리) holds standardized charts from participating hospitals. Its registration table, cncr_rgst, is each hospital's own record.
  • The combined library (K-CURE 라이브러리) links the clinical library to the Cancer Public Library for people in both.
  • Specialized data (특화 데이터) are 67 hospital-built datasets, often images or a single hospital's cohort.
  • Health and medical data (보건의료 데이터) are open files from the Ministry and a person-level link of nine institutions.

Eligibility, premiums, and claims also appear in the NHIS research databases, for a population sample. Their names and codes can differ, so read codes from the K-CURE dictionary for the extract in hand.

docs.title: Combined library (K-CURE 라이브러리)
docs.text:
The portal uses "K-CURE library" for three arrangements of the same two sources: the clinical library alone, the Cancer Public Library alone, and the two linked at the person level.

Source

The three-way definition follows the portal's K-CURE library overview.

Arrangement What a study gets Clinical Hospital charts, standardized, for participating hospitals Public The national registry cohort, with claims, screening, death, and, in current builds, COVID-19 Clinical and public Both, on the people who can be linked

The third arrangement is the one that puts chart-level stage, pathology, and results next to the national claims and death records. It is requested on the combined-data path (결합 데이터 신청), not by applying for the two libraries separately and merging them. Researchers do not hold the key that would make that merge possible. Linkage is done inside the project, as described on the project page.

The library overview also describes the public-library samples on the same page. Those samples are public data only. They are documented on the sample page.

This site does not yet have a separate description of how a combined extract is reviewed, which hospitals can be linked, or how often a registered patient matches a contributing hospital. Those facts belong here once an official guide or an approved project records them.

docs.title: Health and medical data (보건의료 데이터)
docs.text:
The portal's fourth data menu is not a cancer database. It points at two public-data services run for the Ministry of Health and Welfare.

Source

This page follows the portal's health-data overview and the home-page count of nine institutions, viewed on 29 October 2026.

  • Open health data. Files, images, and video that the Ministry publishes for reuse. These are posted objects, not a person-level research extract, so they have no variable list on this site unless a particular file turns out to be one.
  • Health and medical big data (보건의료 빅데이터). Person-level linkage of data from nine institutions, released to researchers for public-purpose studies. That linkage does need a variable list. It is the platform's own documentation, not the Cancer Public Library dictionary. The safe-use center FAQ also points approved users to the Health and Medical Big Data Platform for reservations.

The nine institutions are not named on the overview page this summary follows. A cancer study does not receive the registry by applying here. Registry studies use the Cancer Public Library. This menu matters when a project needs a public file the cancer library does not carry, or when the work is approved on the big-data platform and then booked into a center that also serves K-CURE.

docs.title: Sources and versions
docs.text: This site describes the Cancer Public Library as data dictionary version 4.0 (자료설명서 Ver 4.0, September 2026, with crosswalk version 2.0) describes it. Other official pages give older years and counts. This page lines them up, so that a figure seen elsewhere can be placed.

docs.title: Current description
docs.text:
Dictionary version 4.0 describes the build as of June 2026:

  • registry diagnoses from 2012 through 2022, about 2.92 million registrations, with a person who has two cancers counted twice;
  • NHIS and HIRA files from 2007 through 2024;
  • deaths from 2012 through 2023;
  • COVID-19 confirmations and vaccinations from 2020 through 2023.

The samples follow the portal's data catalogs, downloaded 30 October 2026.

docs.title: Other figures
docs.text:
Source Diagnosis years Count Data dictionary version 4.0 (September 2026) 2012–2022 About 2.92 million registrations Public-library overview on the portal 2012–2022 2,923,903 people Portal home page, 29 October 2026 Not stated About 2.26 million people Choi et al., 2024, describing the first release 2012–2019 1,983,499 people Portal FAQ 2012–2019 Not stated

No official page explains how the home-page figure is counted. The 2024 profile and the FAQ describe the first release, in which claims began in 2012. The current library starts claims in 2007, so the years before a diagnosis are observed.

docs.title: Samples
docs.text: The catalog page lists six site samples (stomach, breast, colorectal, liver, lung, pancreas) and five staging samples (stomach, breast, colorectal, liver, lung). The library overview also names kidney and prostate samples, and the catalog page has no workbook for them. The sample page describes both kinds.

docs.title: Specialized data (특화 데이터)
docs.text:
Specialized data are research datasets built by the medical-data-centered hospitals (의료데이터 중심병원). They are organized by disease and by hospital, and they include material the public library never has, such as images, waveforms, and curated clinical tables. The portal home page, on 29 October 2026, counted 67 of them.

Sources

The definition and the application steps follow the portal's specialized-data page. The hospital program that produces the datasets is described on the portal's medical-data-centered hospital page. The count of 67 follows the portal home page on 29 October 2026.

docs.title: What they cover
docs.text:
The portal describes the program as building high-quality Korean datasets for research and for training models, in cancer, circulatory disease, and respiratory disease including COVID-19, plus other disease-, age-, and patient-group sets. A consortium page lists, as examples, cancer imaging and endoscopy, brain MRI, intensive-care waveforms, chest X-ray, and pathology slides. Each dataset has its own hospital, years, patient count, and table count. This site does not yet reproduce that catalog.

These datasets are not the Cancer Public Library and not the national clinical-library schema. A lung-cancer image set from one consortium is that consortium's files. It does not contain the national registry, unless the dataset's own description says it was linked.

docs.title: How access works
docs.text:
The portal lists six steps, and they differ from the public-library timetable.

  1. Read the dataset overview, the items, and the application rules on the portal.
  2. Apply under the providing institution's procedure.
  3. The providing institution reviews release. Moving the data to a safe-use center at a different institution is a further review.
  4. Agree the place where the data will be analyzed.
  5. Analyze, and request export of the results.
  6. The institution that runs the analysis room reviews the export.

A study that only needs the national registry should use the Cancer Public Library. A study that needs images or a hospital's curated cohort uses this menu, and has to read that dataset's own page.

docs.title: Clinical library (임상 라이브러리)
docs.text:
The clinical library is a separate database from the Cancer Public Library. It is standardized electronic medical record data from hospitals that participate in K-CURE. It holds the clinical detail the public library does not: pathology, laboratory results, imaging, drugs as ordered in the hospital, and follow-up recorded in the chart. It covers the patients of those hospitals, not every registered cancer patient in Korea.

Sources

Definitions follow the portal's clinical-library overview. Counts that disagree with that page are taken from the portal home page on 29 October 2026 and from the portal FAQ. The schema is the public ClinicalLibrary repository.

docs.title: Two databases
docs.text:
The overview splits the library in two.

  • Baseline DB. Common clinical data, not limited to one disease, mapped from each hospital's clinical data warehouse. The overview says the model has 6 groups and 39 tables and borrows the OMOP common data model. The FAQ says 15 hospitals contribute to Baseline.
  • Cancer clinical library (암 임상 라이브러리). Cancer-specific items, standardized with the relevant clinical societies and then implemented by the participating hospitals. Each cancer has its own schema, arranged in five groups: patient, diagnosis, tests, treatment, and follow-up (환자, 진단, 검사, 치료, 추적관찰), with subgroups that differ by cancer.

The overview also says the clinical library as a whole was planned to cover cancer from 2022 through 2025, and respiratory and cardiovascular disease. This page is about the cancer portion.

docs.title: How many cancers, and how many people
docs.text:
The official pages do not agree, and this site does not pick a winner.

Source What it says Portal home page, 29 October 2026 6 cancer types, about 500,000 people Clinical-library overview 10 cancers, and a plan to build the library with 18 hospitals K-CURE library overview 1.65 million people in standardized clinical data Portal FAQ, written as the state in 2022 Stomach and breast were built. The plan was colorectal and liver by 2023, pancreas, lung, and prostate by 2024, and cervix, kidney, and hematologic cancers by 2025 Same FAQ, on hospitals Baseline, 15 hospitals. Breast, 11 hospitals. Stomach, 6 hospitals

The ten cancers named in that 2022 plan are stomach (위암), breast (유방암), colorectal (대장암), liver (간암), pancreas (췌장암), lung (폐암), prostate (전립선암), cervix (자궁경부암), kidney (신장암), and hematologic cancers (혈액암). The home page's "6 cancer types" is the current advertisement. Which six, and whether the later cancers in the plan were finished, is not stated on the pages above. The application catalog is the place to see what can be requested.

Each hospital decides on the request for its own patients. An approval does not extend to hospitals that did not review it.

docs.title: Tables
docs.text:
The portal points to github.com/k-cure/ClinicalLibrary for the schemas. The repository holds the cancer clinical library, a standard vocabulary, common codes, a cancer-registration table, a statistics database, the Baseline OMOP schema, and a quality-management folder, plus a guide PDF for hospitals building the library. The FAQ says a new schema version goes to participating hospitals first and is published after the build that uses it.

The hospital registration table is cncr_rgst. The Baseline model's 39 tables, and the tables inside each cancer schema, each belong on their own page once that schema is transcribed. They are not listed here in advance of that schema.

docs.title: What it does not replace
docs.text: A clinical-library cohort is the patients whose hospitals contributed charts. Survival, incidence, and treatment patterns from it do not describe Korea. The national cohort, with stage and morphology but without chart-level results, is the Cancer Public Library. A study that needs both on the same people is a combined application.

docs.title: Hospital cancer registration
docs.text:
cncr_rgst is the cancer-registration table in the clinical library. Participating hospitals map a registration into this table. Its key is the hospital, the hospital patient number, the date of the first visit, and a registration sequence. The columns include primary site, laterality, histology, grade, a SEER code, stage, and treatment, stored with the hospital's own identifiers.

The national registry extract is RGST in the Cancer Public Library. cncr_rgst is the hospital file. Its columns are not the column list for a public-library extract.

Source

The schema is the public ClinicalLibrary repository, in the cancer-registration folder.

docs.title: Cancer Public Library (암 공공 라이브러리)
docs.text:
The Cancer Public Library links the national cancer registry to death records, health-insurance eligibility, general health examinations, national cancer screening, health-insurance claims, and COVID-19 records. The portal calls it a full-cycle history (전주기 이력관리형), because it covers care before diagnosis, the diagnosis itself, treatment, and death. This page describes the customized extract. The sample page describes the site samples and staging samples.

At a glance

  • Cohort. Every cancer registered from 2012 through 2022, about 2.92 million registrations, with a person counted once per cancer.
  • Years. Claims, eligibility, checkups, and screening run from 2007 through 2024, so the years before a diagnosis are observed. Deaths run through 2023.
  • Linkage. Every table joins on SN_KEY, and the four claims tables also join on MID.
  • Limits. The library has no cancer-free controls, no uninsured care, and no laboratory values beyond the checkup and screening results.
Sources

The definition and the source institutions follow the portal's public-library overview. The cohort, the table list, and the years follow data dictionary version 4.0 (September 2026, describing the build as of June 2026). The linkage method and the limits follow the data resource profile by Choi and colleagues.1

docs.title: Who is in the library
docs.text:
Membership is a row on RGST, the registry table. The cohort is cancers registered from 2012 through 2022, about 2.92 million registrations. A person with two primary cancers (다중원발암) is counted twice and has two rows on RGST.

People who were never registered with cancer are absent, so the library has no cancer-free comparison group. Counts from the library also differ from the registry's published incidence: the diagnosis years are fixed, and a person with two cancers contributes two rows.

docs.text:

docs.title: How the files are linked
docs.text:
Each source institution creates a linkage key from the resident registration number (주민등록번호), using a secure hash and a salt supplied for the project. A linkage table joins those keys, and the National Cancer Data Center builds the library from it and then deletes it. The released files carry one non-identifying person number, SN_KEY, so the same person can be followed across tables and years.

SN_KEY is reassigned at every extraction, so it identifies a person only within one extract. Researchers cannot link another person-level file themselves. The joins are described in the research note on how the tables fit together.

docs.title: What the library cannot measure
docs.text:
• Care outside national health insurance, such as over-the-counter drugs and uncovered services.
  • Images, laboratory values, and biomarkers, except the results recorded on the checkup and cancer-screening tables.
  • Sensitive conditions, including mental illness, suicide, sexually transmitted diseases, and miscarriage, which are removed or masked.
  • Whether another disease occurred. Diagnoses other than the registry cancer are billing codes.
  • Patient-reported outcomes and the reasons for a treatment choice.

  1. Choi DW, et al. Data Resource Profile: The Cancer Public Library Database in South Korea. Cancer Research and Treatment. 2024;56(4):1014-1026. doi:10.4143/crt.2024.207 ↩

The row joins to the rest of the library on SN_KEY, and to a claim on SN_KEY and the year of care.

docs.title: Breast screening, 2007–2008 (CBR_RST_0708)
docs.text:
CBR_RST_0708 (유방암 검진) is a table in the Cancer Public Library. One row is one breast screening in 2007–2008. The form changed in 2009, so the other period is CBR_RST_0924.

The record covers mammography findings and the location of each lesion, and the judgment. The questionnaire for the same screening is CQ_RST_0708, and the two join on SN_KEY and the examination year EXMD_BZ_YYYY.

The people are those on RGST with a national cancer screening record from 2007 through 2024. When a screening has more than one judgment, the most important one is recorded. Findings can be recorded up to three at a time, in order of severity. Using any screening table requires a research-use plan.

Who is screened. Women aged 40 or older, every 2 years.

docs.title: Death
docs.text:
DEATH (사망) is a table in the Cancer Public Library. One row is one death of a person on RGST, from 2012 through 2023, for 889,536 deaths. A person who was alive at the end of 2023 has no row. The row joins to the rest of the library on SN_KEY.

The variables are listed, each with its own page, in the variable list.

Source

The count, years, and variables follow data dictionary version 4.0, Table 2 and the death-table overview (September 2026).

docs.title: Variables
docs.text:
Variable 한글 Definition DREGDATE 사망연월일 Date of death, YYYYMMDD SAIN1 사망원인코드1 Underlying cause, in the Korean Standard Classification of Diseases (KCD). Sensitive causes in chapters 1 (A00–B99), 5 (F00–F99), 19 (S00–T98), and 20 (V01–Y98) are collapsed to a block, such as V59 to V50–V59 SAIN2 사망원인코드2 External-cause detail (V01–Y98) when SAIN1 is an injury code (S00–T98). The same sensitive-cause collapsing applies

Cause-of-death codes follow the statistics-office notice of 1 July 2020 (국가데이터처 고시 제2020-175호).

docs.title: General checkup target (G1E_OBJ)
docs.text:
G1E_OBJ (일반건강검진 대상자) is a table in the Cancer Public Library. One row is one person in one examination year, from 2007 through 2024. It has two variables besides SN_KEY: the examination year (EXMD_BZ_YYYY) and the work type (WKG_TYPE_CD, 근무구분코드), which decides whether an employee is examined every year.

The questionnaire answers are on G1Q_0708, G1Q_0917, and G1Q_1824, and the measured results are on G1E. All of them join on SN_KEY and EXMD_BZ_YYYY.

The people are those on RGST with a general health examination record from 2007 through 2024. Using any checkup table requires a research-use plan.

Eligible years or examined years

The dictionary defines the people in every checkup table as registered patients with an examination record. It does not say whether G1E_OBJ also lists the years in which a person was eligible and skipped the examination. In the NHIS customized database, a table of the same name lists the eligible population. Within an extract, comparing the years on G1E_OBJ with the years on G1E for the same person settles the question. The National Cancer Data Center (data@ncc.re.kr) can also confirm it.

The variables are listed, each with its own page, in the variable list.

docs.title: Who is examined
docs.text:
Insurance type Who is examined How often Self-employed insured, household head Everyone Every 2 years Self-employed insured, household member Aged 20 or older Every 2 years Employee insured Everyone Every 2 years, or every year for a non-office worker Employee dependent Aged 20 or older Every 2 years Medical Aid, household head Aged 19–64 Every 2 years, from 2012 Medical Aid, household member Aged 40–64 Every 2 years, from 2012 Source

The description follows the health-examination overview in data dictionary version 4.0 (September 2026).

docs.title: Checkup results (G1E)
docs.text:
G1E (일반건강검진 결과 및 판정) is a table in the Cancer Public Library. One row is the measured results of one general health examination, from 2007 through 2024. The questionnaire for the same examination is on G1Q_0708, G1Q_0917, or G1Q_1824, depending on the year, and joins on SN_KEY and EXMD_BZ_YYYY.

The people are those on RGST with a general health examination record from 2007 through 2024. Using any checkup table requires a research-use plan.

docs.title: What is measured
docs.text:
• Body: height, weight, waist, body mass index, and blood pressure.
  • Urine: glucose, protein, and occult blood.
  • Blood: hemoglobin, fasting glucose, total, HDL, and LDL cholesterol, triglycerides, creatinine, eGFR, AST, ALT, and GGT.

Body measures are top- and bottom-coded:

Variable Released as Height (G1E_HGHT) 150 or less, then each centimeter from 151 to 179, then 180 or more Weight (G1E_WGHT) 40 or less, then each kilogram from 41 to 99, then 100 or more Body mass index (G1E_BMI) 18.5 or less, then one decimal from 18.6 to 29.9, then 30 or more Waist (G1E_WSTC) 60 or less, then each centimeter from 61 to 89, then 90 or more

The variables are listed, each with its own page, in the variable list.

docs.title: Who is examined
docs.text:
The general health examination follows the schedule below, so most people have a record every other year at most.

Insurance type Who is examined How often Self-employed insured, household head Everyone Every 2 years Self-employed insured, household member Aged 20 or older Every 2 years Employee insured Everyone Every 2 years, or every year for a non-office worker Employee dependent Aged 20 or older Every 2 years Medical Aid, household head Aged 19–64 Every 2 years, from 2012 Medical Aid, household member Aged 40–64 Every 2 years, from 2012 Source

The description follows the health-examination overview and its pseudonymization table in data dictionary version 4.0 (September 2026).

docs.title: Checkup questionnaire, 2007–2008 (G1Q_0708)
docs.text:
G1Q_0708 (일반건강검진 문진) is a table in the Cancer Public Library. One row is the questionnaire answered at one general health examination in 2007–2008. The form changed over time, so the other years are in G1Q_0917 for 2009–2017 and G1Q_1824 for 2018–2024.

The questionnaire covers disease history, family history, diet, smoking, drinking, physical activity, and stress. The row joins to the rest of the library on SN_KEY, and to the measured results on G1E on SN_KEY and the examination year EXMD_BZ_YYYY.

The people are those on RGST with a general health examination record from 2007 through 2024. Using any checkup table requires a research-use plan.

The variables are listed, each with its own page, in the variable list.

Source

The description follows the health-examination overview in data dictionary version 4.0 (September 2026).

docs.title: Checkup questionnaire, 2009–2017 (G1Q_0917)
docs.text:
G1Q_0917 (일반건강검진 문진) is a table in the Cancer Public Library. One row is the questionnaire answered at one general health examination in 2009–2017. The form changed over time, so the other years are in G1Q_0708 for 2007–2008 and G1Q_1824 for 2018–2024.

The questionnaire covers disease history and treatment, family history, hepatitis B, smoking, drinking, and physical activity. The row joins to the rest of the library on SN_KEY, and to the measured results on G1E on SN_KEY and the examination year EXMD_BZ_YYYY.

The people are those on RGST with a general health examination record from 2007 through 2024. Using any checkup table requires a research-use plan.

The variables are listed, each with its own page, in the variable list.

Source

The description follows the health-examination overview in data dictionary version 4.0 (September 2026).

docs.title: Checkup questionnaire, 2018–2024 (G1Q_1824)
docs.text:
G1Q_1824 (일반건강검진 문진) is a table in the Cancer Public Library. One row is the questionnaire answered at one general health examination in 2018–2024. The form changed over time, so the other years are in G1Q_0708 for 2007–2008 and G1Q_0917 for 2009–2017.

The questionnaire covers disease history and treatment, family history, hepatitis B, smoking, e-cigarettes and heated tobacco, drinking by type of drink, and physical activity. The row joins to the rest of the library on SN_KEY, and to the measured results on G1E on SN_KEY and the examination year EXMD_BZ_YYYY.

The people are those on RGST with a general health examination record from 2007 through 2024. Using any checkup table requires a research-use plan.

The variables are listed, each with its own page, in the variable list.

Source

The description follows the health-examination overview in data dictionary version 4.0 (September 2026).

docs.title: Cancer registration
docs.text:
RGST (암등록) is the registry table of the Cancer Public Library. One row is one registered cancer, diagnosed from 2012 through 2022, for 2,923,903 rows. A person with two cancers has two rows with the same SN_KEY, which joins the row to death, claims, screening, and the other tables.

Source

Variable names, codes, and the row count follow data dictionary version 4.0 (September 2026), Table 1 and the registry-table overview.

docs.title: Variables
docs.text:
RGST has ten variables besides SN_KEY. Each has its own page in the variable list.

Variable 한글 Definition SEX 성별 1 man, 2 woman AGE 진단시 만나이 Age in full years at the first diagnosis date, in bands: 29 and under, five-year groups from 30 to 84, and 85 and older. One-year age requires a research-use plan and committee approval ICD10 국제질병분류코드 Site in ICD-10, without the decimal (C161 for C16.1) TCODE 원발부위코드 Primary site in ICD-O-3 topography, without the decimal MCODE_GRP 조직학적진단그룹 Histology in 17 ICD-O-3 groups. A finer grouping requires a research-use plan FDX 최초진단연월일 Date of first diagnosis, YYYYMMDD TX 치료 Treatment within four months of diagnosis, as five digits of 0 or 1: surgery, chemotherapy, radiation, immunotherapy, hormone therapy. Surgery and radiation is 10100 METHOD 최종진단방법 Most definitive basis of diagnosis. 0 death certificate only, 1 clinical, 2 clinical test, 3 surgery or autopsy without histology, 4 special biochemical or immunological test, 5 cytology or hematology, 6 histology of a metastasis, 7 histology of the primary site, 8 autopsy SEER_GRP 요약병기 SEER summary stage. 0 carcinoma in situ, 1 localized (국한), 2 regional (국소), 7 distant (원격), 9 unknown. A colorectal in situ code (D01.x) can also be coded 1, localized MULTI_9911 '99–'11년 암진단 여부 Y if the person had a cancer diagnosed in 1999–2011, otherwise N

Province of residence is on the eligibility table, BFC, as SIDO_CD. Date and cause of death are on DEATH.

docs.title: Registry diagnoses and claims diagnoses
docs.text:
A claims diagnosis is the code a provider billed, which can be a suspected cancer, a rule-out, or a cancer treated years earlier. RGST records a cancer the registry confirmed, with a date, a site, and a stage. A cohort defined from RGST therefore avoids the false positives and missed cases of a claims-based definition.

TX summarizes treatment within four months. The procedures, drugs, and dates are on the claims tables T200, T300, T400, and T530.

docs.title: Detailed stage
docs.text: SEER_GRP is the only stage variable on the customized RGST. Tumor size, nodes, metastasis, grade, and TNM stage are in the staging samples (표본 병기), for stomach, breast, colorectal, liver, and lung.

docs.title: Sample
docs.text:
The portal releases two kinds of sample, and each one is a separate database, applied for and delivered on its own. A site sample (표본) is about 20 percent of one cancer site. A staging sample (표본 병기) is about 10 percent of one site, and its registration table comes from the registry's staging survey (협력병기). 병기 means stage.

At a glance

  • Site sample. Six sites, with the same registration items as the customized extract (summary stage, histology, treatment) and a shorter list of claims columns.
  • Staging sample. Five sites, whose registration table adds tumor size, nodes, metastasis, grade, and TNM stage, depending on the site.
  • Other tables. Death, eligibility, claims, and checkups are the same in both kinds of sample. Screening is included only for the sample's own site, and COVID-19 is absent.
  • Age and dates. Neither kind lists year of birth. AGE is age at diagnosis in five-year bands, and the diagnosis date is given as year and month.
  • Access. Both are analyzed remotely, on a virtual desktop, and delivered about one month after review.
Sources

The sites and the 20 percent and 10 percent figures follow the portal's K-CURE library overview. The tables and variables follow the data catalogs on the catalog page, downloaded 30 October 2026. The library overview also names kidney and prostate samples, and the catalog page has no workbook for them.

The variable lists are under Variables, for the site samples and the staging samples. Where the samples are analyzed is on Using the data.

docs.title: Site sample (표본)
docs.text:
A site sample's registration table keeps the registry items of the customized extract: SEER summary stage (SEER_GRP), treatment (TX), and basis of diagnosis (METHOD). It stores the full histology code MCODE, where the customized extract stores a 17-group code (MCODE_GRP). It omits MULTI_9911, the flag for a cancer diagnosed in 1999–2011.

Sample 한글 Diagnoses Tables Stomach 위암 표본 2012–2021 16, including stomach screening Breast 유방암 표본 2012–2021 16, including breast screening Colorectal 대장암 표본 2012–2021 16, including colorectal screening Liver 간암 표본 2012–2021 16, including liver screening Lung 폐암 표본 2012–2021 12, without screening Pancreas 췌장암 표본 2012–2021 12, without screening

docs.title: Staging sample (표본 병기)
docs.text:
A staging sample replaces the registration table with the staging-survey record. For stomach, breast, and colorectal cancer, that record has tumor size, nodes, metastasis, grade, and AJCC TNM stage, and it omits SEER_GRP, TX, and the ICD-10 code. Liver and lung have their own stage items.

Sample 한글 Registration table Stage detail Stomach 위암 표본 병기 CS_GC_RGST, 40 variables Tumor size, nodes, metastasis, grade, AJCC TNM Breast 유방암 표본 병기 CS_BC_RGST, 55 variables Tumor size, nodes, metastasis, grade, AJCC TNM, and breast-specific factors Colorectal 대장암 표본 병기 CS_CC_RGST, 41 variables Tumor size, nodes, metastasis, grade, AJCC TNM Liver 간암 표본 병기 CS_LV_RGST, 11 variables Height, weight, AFP, clinical TNM and stage Lung 폐암 표본 병기 CS_LC_RGST, 32 variables Smoking, histology, EGFR, ALK, imaging and pathologic TNM

Diagnoses run from 2012 through 2021, and lung starts in 2014. For stomach, breast, and colorectal, the catalog refers to the Korea Central Cancer Registry's cooperative-staging user guide (협력병기 조사자료 이용자 안내서) for the detailed codes. The code tables on the variable pages are the codes the catalog itself lists.

docs.title: Other tables
docs.text:
The other tables are the same in a site sample and a staging sample of the same cancer. They are the same kinds of record as in the customized extract, with fewer columns.

  • Eligibility omits the number of people on the insurance card.
  • Claim statement omits several fields, including the cost amounts.
  • Services and outpatient prescriptions omit unit price and amount.
  • Checkups are included for every site. The questionnaire for recent years is G1Q_1823, so these files run through 2023.
  • Screening is included only for the sample's own site, in files that run through 2023 (0923). Lung and pancreas have no screening table.
  • COVID-19 is absent.

The catalogs do not list SN_KEY. The claims tables list MID.

docs.title: Age and dates
docs.text: Neither kind of sample lists year of birth. AGE is age at diagnosis, in five-year bands. FDX is the year and month of first diagnosis, where the customized extract gives the full date. DBYEAR (자료등록연도) on a staging table is the year the record was registered.

docs.title: Claim statement (T200)
docs.text:
T200 (명세서 일반내역) is a table in the Cancer Public Library. One row is one reviewed health-insurance claim, from 2007 through 2024, for people on RGST. It is the hub of the claims: T300, T400, and T530 add the lines of the claim and join to it on MID (명세서조인키).

The table has three groups of items:

  • the patient, including age and insurance type;
  • the claim, including the start and end of care, inpatient or outpatient, the primary and secondary diagnoses, and the reviewed cost;
  • the provider, as a replacement provider number.

Main and secondary diagnosis codes follow the same masking as T400. The variables are listed, each with its own page, in the variable list.

Source

The description follows the claims-table overview in data dictionary version 4.0 (September 2026).

docs.title: Services (T300)
docs.text:
T300 (진료내역) is a table in the Cancer Public Library. One row is one service line on a claim: a procedure, a treatment material, or a drug given inside the institution. The years are 2007–2024, for people on RGST with a reviewed claim. The row joins to its claim on T200 on MID (명세서조인키).

Procedure codes are released in full, and material codes are shortened to the first five characters. A full material code and the cost variables require a research-use plan.

DY1_MDCT_QTY (1일투약량) is the number of doses per day, and the amount per dose is a separate variable. Total use is the amount per dose times the doses per day times the number of days.

The variables are listed, each with its own page, in the variable list.

Source

The description follows the claims-table overview and the variable notes in data dictionary version 4.0 (September 2026).

docs.title: Diagnoses on the claim (T400)
docs.text:
T400 (상병내역) is a table in the Cancer Public Library. One row is one diagnosis on a claim, primary or secondary, with the specialty. The years are 2007–2024, for people on RGST with a reviewed claim. The row joins to its claim on T200 on MID (명세서조인키).

These diagnosis codes are billing codes, stored up to four characters. Sensitive diagnoses are masked:

  • Mental illness is reduced to its first character followed by asterisks, so F00 becomes F**. A three-character code requires a research-use plan and committee approval.
  • Rare diseases and sexually transmitted infections are masked entirely.
  • Claims for HIV, miscarriage, abuse, and COVID-19 are removed.

The variables are listed, each with its own page, in the variable list.

Source

The description follows the claims-table overview and the pseudonymization table in data dictionary version 4.0 (September 2026).

docs.title: Outpatient prescriptions (T530)
docs.text:
T530 (원외처방내역) is a table in the Cancer Public Library. One row is one drug prescribed to be dispensed outside the institution. Drugs given inside the institution are on T300. The years are 2007–2024, for people on RGST with a reviewed claim. The row joins to its claim on T200 on MID (명세서조인키).

The ingredient code (GNL_CD) is shortened. A research-use plan that covers dose, route, or formulation releases all eight characters. Cost variables also require a research-use plan.

DY1_MDCT_QTY (1일투약량) is the number of doses per day. For an ointment, for example, the dose per day and the days of use are both recorded as 1.

The variables are listed, each with its own page, in the variable list.

Source

The description follows the claims-table overview and the variable notes in data dictionary version 4.0 (September 2026).

docs.title: Program and data
docs.text:
K-CURE is a portal with several data products. The cancer registry that most registry studies need is part of the Cancer Public Library, which is the focus of this site.

  • The K-CURE project describes who runs the project and the legal basis for releasing pseudonymized cancer data.
  • What the portal releases lists the products and the three databases in the Cancer Public Library.
  • Applying for data covers eligibility, documents, the review timetable, and fees.
  • Using the data covers where each database is analyzed, the period of use, the safe-use centers, and export review.

docs.title: Applying for data
docs.text:
The Cancer Public Library is requested through the portal's public-data application (공공데이터 신청) and reviewed by the National Cancer Data Center. This page describes that application. Where the approved data are analyzed is on Using the data.

At a glance

  • Who can apply. The principal investigator must be a Korean national living in Korea, and every member who will use the data needs a portal account.
  • Documents. Every application includes a research-use plan, a data specification, and an IRB or DRB approval.
  • Minimum data. Request only the variables the study will use, and attach a research-use plan for restricted items such as one-year age.
  • Timetable. Applications are reviewed in the month after they arrive. Delivery then takes about three months for a customized extract and about one month for a sample.
  • Fees. The data fee starts at 200,000 won for up to 20 GB, and public bodies, universities, and thesis projects qualify for reductions on the other fees.
Sources

This page follows the portal's public-data application page and its English counterpart, data dictionary version 4.0 (September 2026, pages 3–7 of the overview), and the data resource profile by Choi and colleagues,1 which describes what the review committees check.

docs.title: Who can apply
docs.text:
• The principal investigator must be a Korean national living in Korea.
  • The principal investigator and everyone who will use the analysis environment must already have a portal account.
  • A thesis project must also register the thesis author.

docs.title: Documents
docs.text:
Every application attaches three documents:

  • a research-use plan (연구활용계획서),
  • a data specification (데이터 명세서), listing the tables and variables requested, and
  • an IRB or DRB approval (IRB/DRB 승인 확인서).

Using the personal-information innovation zone at the National Cancer Center requires an extra application form, a research-use plan, and a business registration certificate. That zone is handled by the center's data linkage team.

docs.title: What the committee checks
docs.text:
Two committees review an application: the data-provision review committee (데이터제공심의위원회) and the data-export review committee (데이터반출심사위원회). In principle, only the minimum data needed for the question are released, so request only the variables the study will use. A request for unrelated data can be rejected.

Some items are released only with a research-use plan that justifies them, and some also need committee approval. Examples are one-year age on RGST, three-character mental-illness codes, full drug ingredient codes, and the checkup, screening, and COVID-19 tables. Each dataset page notes its restricted items.

docs.title: Timetable
docs.text:
Applications received by the last day of a month are reviewed the following month. From the review date, a customized extract takes about three months to deliver, and a sample takes about one month.

Progress appears under 나의연구 (My Research) on the portal and is also sent by email and text message, so the account must allow those messages. A change to an approved study is made through a change request on the same application.

The approval lasts two years from the start of analysis: up to one year of analysis, then up to one year of storage. Using the same data after that requires a new application.

docs.title: Fees and reductions
docs.text:
The data fee is 200,000 won for a SAS dataset of up to 20 GB, plus 10,000 won for each additional gigabyte, up to 500 GB. The dictionary marks this 200,000 won base fee as not eligible for reductions. The fee for the analysis platform is charged separately and is described on Using the data.

The dictionary also lists reductions on the data and platform fees. Government bodies, public institutions, public health institutions, and researchers under contract to them pay nothing or a reduced fee. A thesis project gets 80 percent off the data fee and 50 percent off the platform fee. Universities, medical institutions, and academic societies also qualify for a reduction. The full table is on page 7 of the dictionary.

Questions about the application, the build, the review, delivery, and payment go to the National Cancer Data Center (data@ncc.re.kr, 031-920-2597).

docs.title: Other products
docs.text:
The clinical library, combined data, specialized data, and health data each have their own application. A clinical-library request is reviewed by each hospital whose data are requested. A combined extract uses the combined-data application (결합 데이터 신청). Specialized datasets are requested from the hospital that built them. Those routes are sketched on the clinical library, combined library, specialized data, and health data pages.

  1. Choi DW, et al. Data Resource Profile: The Cancer Public Library Database in South Korea. Cancer Research and Treatment. 2024;56(4):1014-1026. doi:10.4143/crt.2024.207 ↩

docs.title: What the portal releases
docs.text:
The portal's data menu has four products. The cancer registry is part of the first one, the Cancer Public Library, which is the focus of this site.

At a glance

  • Four products. These are the Cancer Public Library, the clinical library, specialized data, and health and medical data.
  • The registry. National registry records reach a study only through the Cancer Public Library.
  • Three databases. The Cancer Public Library is released as a customized extract, a site sample, or a staging sample, and each is applied for on its own.
Sources

The four products and the counts follow the portal home page as viewed on 29 October 2026. The definitions follow each product's overview page. Other official pages give different counts, and those are lined up on Sources and versions.

docs.title: The four products
docs.text:
Product 한글 What it is Portal summary, 29 Oct 2026 Cancer Public Library 암 공공 라이브러리 Every registered cancer patient, with registry, death, claims, screening, and COVID-19 records linked About 2.26 million people Clinical library 임상 라이브러리 Standardized electronic records from participating hospitals 6 cancer types, about 500,000 people Specialized data 특화 데이터 Disease-specific datasets built by hospitals, including images 67 datasets Health and medical data 보건의료 데이터 Open health files, and a person-level link of nine institutions' data 9 institutions

The portal also uses the name K-CURE library (K-CURE 라이브러리) for clinical data, public data, or the two linked together.

docs.title: Where the registry is
docs.text:
The Cancer Public Library is built from the Korea Central Cancer Registry. Its cohort is every registered cancer, and the registry items travel with that cohort into every extract. A study that needs incidence, site, histology, or stage, followed by claims or death, applies for this library.

The clinical library has its own registration table, cncr_rgst, which is each hospital's record of its own patients. The national registry table is RGST.

docs.title: Three databases in the Cancer Public Library
docs.text:
Database 한글 Who is in it Where it is analyzed Customized extract 맞춤형 Every registered cancer, 2012–2022, all sites In person, at a safe-use center Site sample 표본 About 20 percent of one listed site Remote virtual desktop Staging sample 표본 병기 About 10 percent of one listed site, with detailed stage items Remote virtual desktop

The datasets page compares their contents, and Using the data describes the two ways of analyzing them.

docs.title: The K-CURE project
docs.text:
K-CURE (Korean Clinical Data Utilization Network for Research Excellence, 케이큐어) is a Ministry of Health and Welfare project that links the cancer registry to other public health data and to hospital records, and lets approved studies analyze the result inside a closed environment. Its public face is the K-CURE portal.

At a glance

  • Purpose. The project puts registry, insurance, screening, and death records on one person identifier, so a study can follow a registered cancer from screening to death.
  • Who runs it. The National Cancer Data Center builds and releases the Cancer Public Library, and the Korea Health Information Service runs the portal and the central safe-use center.
  • Legal basis. The Cancer Control Act and the Personal Information Protection Act allow the release of pseudonymized data for research.
  • Contacts. Questions about the Cancer Public Library go to data@ncc.re.kr, and questions about the portal and the centers go to k-cure@khis.kr.
Sources

This page follows the portal's service overview, the National Cancer Data Center description of its designation, data dictionary version 4.0 (September 2026), and the data resource profile by Choi and colleagues.1 The profile names the Korea Health Information Service as the party that builds the linkage table, and the portal overview describes the Ministry as receiving the linkage keys. Both say the released file carries only a project-specific person number.

docs.title: What the project does
docs.text:
Each source holds one part of a cancer patient's history. The Korea Central Cancer Registry (중앙암등록본부) records who was diagnosed, with which cancer, and at what stage. The National Health Insurance Service (국민건강보험공단, NHIS) and the Health Insurance Review and Assessment Service (건강보험심사평가원, HIRA) record eligibility, checkups, screening, and claims. The national data office (국가데이터처) records deaths, and the Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency (질병관리청) records COVID-19 cases and vaccinations.

K-CURE links these files on one person identifier, under the rules for pseudonymized data. The linked file stays in a closed analysis environment, and only reviewed results leave it.

docs.title: Who operates it
docs.text:
Role 한글 What it does Ministry of Health and Welfare 보건복지부 Runs the project National Cancer Data Center 국가암데이터센터 Builds, reviews, and releases the Cancer Public Library. Hosted by the National Cancer Center (국립암센터). Contact: data@ncc.re.kr, 031-920-2597 Korea Central Cancer Registry 중앙암등록본부 Supplies the registry file on which the library is built Korea Health Information Service 한국보건의료정보원 Operates the portal and the central safe-use center. Fee payment for the Cancer Public Library also goes through data@ncc.re.kr.

docs.title: Legal basis
docs.text:
Two laws allow the release.

  • The Cancer Control Act (암관리법), article 9-2, establishes the cancer-data program. Under it, the National Cancer Data Center collects records held by public institutions, processes them internally, and provides them for public-interest research.
  • The Personal Information Protection Act (개인정보 보호법) allows pseudonymized data to be used for statistics and scientific research without individual consent.

Each source institution creates a linkage key from the resident registration number, and a linkage table joins those keys. The released file carries one project-specific person number, SN_KEY (대체식별키). Researchers cannot attach another person-level file themselves.

docs.title: What the name covers
docs.text:
The portal uses "K-CURE" for the project, the website, and a library that combines clinical and public data. On this site, K-CURE means the project and the portal, and each released database is named on its own page.

  1. Choi DW, et al. Data Resource Profile: The Cancer Public Library Database in South Korea. Cancer Research and Treatment. 2024;56(4):1014-1026. doi:10.4143/crt.2024.207 ↩

docs.title: Using the data
docs.text:
Researchers never take the Cancer Public Library home. A customized extract is analyzed in person at a safe-use center, and a sample is analyzed on a remote virtual desktop. In both cases, results leave only after they pass export review (반출심사). Applying is a separate step, described on Applying for data.

At a glance

  • Where. A customized extract opens only at a safe-use center, and a site sample or a staging sample opens remotely from the researcher's own computer.
  • How long. An approval lasts two years from the start of analysis: up to one year of analysis and up to one year of storage.
  • Fees. The platform fee is charged by days, weeks, and months of use, and storage is free for the first three months.
  • Reuse during storage. A stored extract can be reopened for up to seven days at a time, booked at least two weeks ahead.
  • Centers. There is a central center in Seoul, a center at the National Cancer Center in Goyang, and seven regional centers, and the statistical software differs by center.
  • Results. Results leave only after export review, and researchers cannot link another person-level file.
Sources

Access modes, fees, and the period of use follow data dictionary version 4.0 (September 2026, pages 4–6 of the overview). Remote access for the staging samples follows the National Cancer Center press release of August 2023. The virtual-desktop drive, software, and reservations follow the portal FAQ. The centers follow the portal's safe-use center page and its English version. The rule against further linkage follows Choi and colleagues.1

docs.title: Access mode by dataset
docs.text:
Dataset 한글 Access mode Where the analysis runs Time from the review date Customized extract 맞춤형 In person A designated safe-use center (안심활용센터), or the personal-information innovation zone at the National Cancer Center About three months Site sample 표본 Remote A virtual desktop (가상PC) assigned to the project, reached from the researcher's own computer About one month Staging sample 표본 병기 Remote A virtual desktop (가상PC) assigned to the project, reached from the researcher's own computer About one month

The dictionary lists both an analysis room and a virtual computer for a customized extract, and a virtual computer alone for a sample. The portal FAQ says the project's source data are on the D drive of its virtual desktop (VDI).

The portal does not say whether remote access uses a VPN or which client software it needs. Those are questions for k-cure@khis.kr.

The personal-information innovation zone (개인정보 이노베이션 존) is a more secure room at the National Cancer Center, with fingerprint and entry authentication and CCTV. Researchers there can analyze data with lighter pseudonymization. Applying for the zone needs extra documents, listed on Applying for data.

docs.title: Period of use and fees
docs.text:
An approval lasts two years from the start of analysis: up to one year of analysis, then up to one year of storage. Using the same data after either limit requires a new application and review.

The analysis-platform fee is half an analysis-room fee and half a virtual-computer fee. The room fee is paid to the center the researcher chooses, and regional centers can set their own room fees. Both are charged by the length of use:

Period of use Fee 6 days or fewer 50,000 won per day 1 week or more 225,000 won per week, plus 50,000 won per remaining day 1 month or more 700,000 won per month, plus 225,000 won per remaining week and 50,000 won per remaining day

Storage is free for three months and then costs 10,000 won per month, up to twelve months.

A GPU server is available at the National Cancer Data Center's center and by remote access. It runs only a Python Jupyter environment and costs twice the virtual-computer fee. Ask the data provision staff first whether it is available. The fee for the innovation zone is set separately.

docs.title: Reuse during storage
docs.text:
Within the approval period, a stored extract can be reopened (보관 중 재사용).

  • Each reuse lasts up to seven days. For a sample, weekends count toward the seven days. For a customized extract, only weekdays count.
  • Agree the start date with the National Cancer Center data provision staff at least two weeks ahead, and file a use request on the portal so the center visit can be scheduled.
  • From the second reuse on, attach evidence such as a journal's revision or rejection email.
  • The same fees and reductions apply as for the analysis platform.

docs.title: Safe-use centers
docs.text:
A safe-use center provides the data and a closed analysis environment for scientific and academic work. Regional centers let researchers outside Seoul use the data. A visit requires an approval and a reservation, which is made through the K-CURE portal or the Health and Medical Big Data Platform.

docs.title: Software
docs.text:
Every center has document tools (Hangul, Excel, Word, PowerPoint). Statistical software differs by center.

Center Statistical software Central center SAS, R, SPSS, Stata, Python National Cancer Data Center SAS, R, Python

A study that depends on a particular package should confirm it with k-cure@khis.kr for the center that will hold the extract.

docs.title: Hours
docs.text:
The National Cancer Data Center's center is open on weekdays from 08:30 to 16:30. The central center is open on weekdays and closed for lunch from 12:00 to 13:00, and it is also closed on public holidays, Labor Day, and the Korea Health Information Service anniversary (24 September). Its opening hours differ across the portal's pages, so check them before booking.

Central-center hours by source Source Central center Korean center page Weekdays 10:00–17:00, closed 12:00–13:00 English center page Weekdays 09:00–18:00, closed 12:00–13:00 Portal FAQ Weekdays 09:00–18:00

docs.title: Results and linkage
docs.text:
Results leave through export review (반출심사). The contributing page explains what that means for anything published from an extract, including notes sent to this site.

Each person has one non-identifying number, shared across the tables, and researchers cannot link any further person-level data themselves. Another linkage has to be built by an institution authorized under the Personal Information Protection Act. A study that needs a file the library lacks should be designed as a linkage project from the start.

  1. Choi DW, et al. Data Resource Profile: The Cancer Public Library Database in South Korea. Cancer Research and Treatment. 2024;56(4):1014-1026. doi:10.4143/crt.2024.207 ↩

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
Person identifier. This substitute identifier links a row in this table to the same person in the other Cancer Public Library tables.

Data dictionary version 4.0, section 10, says the whole file from the five institutions is linked by SN_KEY (대체식별키).

The quality-control section says each table's substitute identifier is replaced with a new serial number every time the data are extracted. An SN_KEY from one extract does not identify the same person in another extract.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
Person identifier. This substitute identifier links a row in this table to the same person in the other Cancer Public Library tables.

Data dictionary version 4.0, section 10, says the whole file from the five institutions is linked by SN_KEY (대체식별키).

The quality-control section says each table's substitute identifier is replaced with a new serial number every time the data are extracted. An SN_KEY from one extract does not identify the same person in another extract.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
Person identifier. This substitute identifier links a row in this table to the same person in the other Cancer Public Library tables.

Data dictionary version 4.0, section 10, says the whole file from the five institutions is linked by SN_KEY (대체식별키).

The quality-control section says each table's substitute identifier is replaced with a new serial number every time the data are extracted. An SN_KEY from one extract does not identify the same person in another extract.

  • Dataset Cancer Public Library (암 공공 라이브러리)
  • Table Colorectal screening, 2007–2008 · 대장암 검진

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
Person identifier. This substitute identifier links a row in this table to the same person in the other Cancer Public Library tables.

Data dictionary version 4.0, section 10, says the whole file from the five institutions is linked by SN_KEY (대체식별키).

The quality-control section says each table's substitute identifier is replaced with a new serial number every time the data are extracted. An SN_KEY from one extract does not identify the same person in another extract.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
Person identifier. This substitute identifier links a row in this table to the same person in the other Cancer Public Library tables.

Data dictionary version 4.0, section 10, says the whole file from the five institutions is linked by SN_KEY (대체식별키).

The quality-control section says each table's substitute identifier is replaced with a new serial number every time the data are extracted. An SN_KEY from one extract does not identify the same person in another extract.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
Person identifier. This substitute identifier links a row in this table to the same person in the other Cancer Public Library tables.

Data dictionary version 4.0, section 10, says the whole file from the five institutions is linked by SN_KEY (대체식별키).

The quality-control section says each table's substitute identifier is replaced with a new serial number every time the data are extracted. An SN_KEY from one extract does not identify the same person in another extract.

  • Table Cancer screening questionnaire, 2007–2008 · 암문진

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
Person identifier. This substitute identifier links a row in this table to the same person in the other Cancer Public Library tables.

Data dictionary version 4.0, section 10, says the whole file from the five institutions is linked by SN_KEY (대체식별키).

The quality-control section says each table's substitute identifier is replaced with a new serial number every time the data are extracted. An SN_KEY from one extract does not identify the same person in another extract.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
Person identifier. This substitute identifier links a row in this table to the same person in the other Cancer Public Library tables.

Data dictionary version 4.0, section 10, says the whole file from the five institutions is linked by SN_KEY (대체식별키).

The quality-control section says each table's substitute identifier is replaced with a new serial number every time the data are extracted. An SN_KEY from one extract does not identify the same person in another extract.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
Person identifier. This substitute identifier links a row in this table to the same person in the other Cancer Public Library tables.

Data dictionary version 4.0, section 10, says the whole file from the five institutions is linked by SN_KEY (대체식별키).

The quality-control section says each table's substitute identifier is replaced with a new serial number every time the data are extracted. An SN_KEY from one extract does not identify the same person in another extract.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
Person identifier. This substitute identifier links a row in this table to the same person in the other Cancer Public Library tables.

Data dictionary version 4.0, section 10, says the whole file from the five institutions is linked by SN_KEY (대체식별키).

The quality-control section says each table's substitute identifier is replaced with a new serial number every time the data are extracted. An SN_KEY from one extract does not identify the same person in another extract.

docs.text:
대체식별키 · Person identifier

  • Dataset Cancer Public Library (암 공공 라이브러리)
  • Table Checkup questionnaire, 2009–2017 · 일반건강검진 문진
  • File G1Q_0917

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
Person identifier. This substitute identifier links a row in this table to the same person in the other Cancer Public Library tables.

Data dictionary version 4.0, section 10, says the whole file from the five institutions is linked by SN_KEY (대체식별키).

The quality-control section says each table's substitute identifier is replaced with a new serial number every time the data are extracted. An SN_KEY from one extract does not identify the same person in another extract.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
Person identifier. This substitute identifier links a row in this table to the same person in the other Cancer Public Library tables.

Data dictionary version 4.0, section 10, says the whole file from the five institutions is linked by SN_KEY (대체식별키).

Lines of the same claim also join T200, T300, T400, and T530 on MID (명세서조인키).

The quality-control section says each table's substitute identifier is replaced with a new serial number every time the data are extracted. An SN_KEY from one extract does not identify the same person in another extract.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
Person identifier. This substitute identifier links a row in this table to the same person in the other Cancer Public Library tables.

Data dictionary version 4.0, section 10, says the whole file from the five institutions is linked by SN_KEY (대체식별키).

Lines of the same claim also join T200, T300, T400, and T530 on MID (명세서조인키).

The quality-control section says each table's substitute identifier is replaced with a new serial number every time the data are extracted. An SN_KEY from one extract does not identify the same person in another extract.

docs.title: Breast sample
docs.text:
유방암 표본. 16 tables, 461 variables in the portal catalog.

This is a site sample (표본). It is its own database: one cancer site, with the tables listed below. The staging sample of the same site, where the catalog has one, is a separate database. How the two differ is on the sample page.

The registration table keeps summary stage (SEER_GRP) and the histology code MCODE. Death, eligibility, claims, and the checkup use the same kind of row as the customized library, with fewer columns. There is no COVID-19 table. A screening table appears here only for a site the catalog includes, and only for this site. The checkup and screening year files in this catalog run through 2023.

Year of birth is not a variable. AGE is age at diagnosis.

On the code sheet, recorded validity runs from 2007 through 2023.

The catalog does not list SN_KEY. Claim lines list MID.

docs.title: Colorectal sample
docs.text:
대장암 표본. 16 tables, 543 variables in the portal catalog.

This is a site sample (표본). It is its own database: one cancer site, with the tables listed below. The staging sample of the same site, where the catalog has one, is a separate database. How the two differ is on the sample page.

The registration table keeps summary stage (SEER_GRP) and the histology code MCODE. Death, eligibility, claims, and the checkup use the same kind of row as the customized library, with fewer columns. There is no COVID-19 table. A screening table appears here only for a site the catalog includes, and only for this site. The checkup and screening year files in this catalog run through 2023.

Year of birth is not a variable. AGE is age at diagnosis.

On the code sheet, recorded validity runs from 2007 through 2023.

The catalog does not list SN_KEY. Claim lines list MID.

docs.title: Liver sample
docs.text:
간암 표본. 16 tables, 497 variables in the portal catalog.

This is a site sample (표본). It is its own database: one cancer site, with the tables listed below. The staging sample of the same site, where the catalog has one, is a separate database. How the two differ is on the sample page.

The registration table keeps summary stage (SEER_GRP) and the histology code MCODE. Death, eligibility, claims, and the checkup use the same kind of row as the customized library, with fewer columns. There is no COVID-19 table. A screening table appears here only for a site the catalog includes, and only for this site. The checkup and screening year files in this catalog run through 2023.

Year of birth is not a variable. AGE is age at diagnosis.

On the code sheet, recorded validity runs from 2007 through 2023.

The catalog does not list SN_KEY. Claim lines list MID.

docs.text:
폐암 표본. 12 tables, 235 variables in the portal catalog.

This is a site sample (표본). It is its own database: one cancer site, with the tables listed below. The staging sample of the same site, where the catalog has one, is a separate database. How the two differ is on the sample page.

The registration table keeps summary stage (SEER_GRP) and the histology code MCODE. Death, eligibility, claims, and the checkup use the same kind of row as the customized library, with fewer columns. There is no COVID-19 table. A screening table appears here only for a site the catalog includes, and only for this site. The checkup and screening year files in this catalog run through 2023.

Year of birth is not a variable. AGE is age at diagnosis.

On the code sheet, recorded validity runs from 2007 through 2023.

The catalog does not list SN_KEY. Claim lines list MID.

췌장암 표본. 12 tables, 235 variables in the portal catalog.

This is a site sample (표본). It is its own database: one cancer site, with the tables listed below. The catalog has no staging sample for this site. How the two differ is on the sample page.

The registration table keeps summary stage (SEER_GRP) and the histology code MCODE. Death, eligibility, claims, and the checkup use the same kind of row as the customized library, with fewer columns. There is no COVID-19 table. A screening table appears here only for a site the catalog includes, and only for this site. The checkup and screening year files in this catalog run through 2023.

Year of birth is not a variable. AGE is age at diagnosis.

On the code sheet, recorded validity runs from 2007 through 2023.

The catalog does not list SN_KEY. Claim lines list MID.

docs.text:
위암 표본. 16 tables, 528 variables in the portal catalog.

This is a site sample (표본). It is its own database: one cancer site, with the tables listed below. The staging sample of the same site, where the catalog has one, is a separate database. How the two differ is on the sample page.

The registration table keeps summary stage (SEER_GRP) and the histology code MCODE. Death, eligibility, claims, and the checkup use the same kind of row as the customized library, with fewer columns. There is no COVID-19 table. A screening table appears here only for a site the catalog includes, and only for this site. The checkup and screening year files in this catalog run through 2023.

Year of birth is not a variable. AGE is age at diagnosis.

On the code sheet, recorded validity runs from 2007 through 2023.

The catalog does not list SN_KEY. Claim lines list MID.

docs.text: Variables

docs.title: Breast staging sample
docs.text:
유방암 표본 병기. 16 tables, 507 variables in the portal catalog.

This is a staging sample (표본 병기). 병기 means stage. It is a separate database from the site sample. Death, eligibility, claims, the checkup, and screening, where this catalog includes them, match the site sample. The registration table is the staging-survey record for this site. How the two databases differ is on the sample page.

DBYEAR (자료등록연도) is the year the record was registered. It is not the year of birth. AGE is age at diagnosis. FDX on this table is the year and month of the first diagnosis.

※ 상세코드는 중앙암등록본부 협력병기 조사자료 이용자 안내서 참고

On the code sheet, recorded validity runs from 2007 through 2023.

The catalog does not list SN_KEY. Claim lines list MID.
